---
title: "Lessons"
---

One solution booklet per paper. A TMUA paper is 20 questions in 75 minutes, which fits a two-hour
session with room to teach, so **"2019 Paper 1" is one lesson** — and Paper 1 and Paper 2 are never
mixed into the same session, because they test genuinely different things.

| Paper | Booklet |
|---|---|
| **2019 Paper 1** | **[Class material](2019_paper1/class_material.qmd)** — all 20 questions, with working space (prints one question per page) |

## What the class material is

Not a mark scheme. A mark scheme tells you the answer; this tells you **how the question was meant to be
read**. Each question has three parts:

- **The topic**, named in a line — what the question is testing, before you see any working.
- **Commentary**, in prose, *before* the solution and readable without spoiling it: what the question is
  really asking, which of the given facts is doing the work, and where the short route is.
- **The solution**, in a collapsible toggle, written as continuous mathematical argument rather than a
  column of algebra — with the reasoning behind each step said out loud.

Each question then closes with **where the wrong options come from**. The four distractors in a TMUA
question are not random: each is the answer produced by a specific, common, entirely reasonable
mistake. A student who understands *which* slip produces option C has learned more than one who merely
knows the answer is B.

The booklet is written to be read aloud — the tutor teaches straight from it. The things that repeat
every session (session shape, phrases, pronunciation, prompts) live once in `TEACHING_GUIDE.md` at the
repository root.
